posts.author: CriticalHit
posts.body: Hi, I've been using RPG Maker XP for over a decade. I recently reinstalled Windows 11 on my computer and am having to re-activate RPG Maker XP. I downloaded the trial, and put in my email and product key. I keep getting an error when then clicking 'activate'. It says my product key is invalid when I've used it many times before when having to re-install RMXP in the past. I also can't find any technical support contact info to contact anyone regarding this. What should I do in order to get my copy of RPG Maker XP activated?

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
depending where you bought the XP from forum or steam, there is a support
button on the top where you can contact or support.
that should help, and follow the instructions there to help or activate.
also double check that you use the correct email and code to activate
and not have a space included that could fail the activating part.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
I haven't run into this myself (been using the Steam version for a while now, for ease of changing computers) but there are a couple of threads that might help you.
It's actually possible that you originally purchased long enough ago that your key may no longer be supported. If you’ve been using XP since before 2013 (-high fives-) then it's possible that
the announcement in this thread
may apply to you. There's
this more recent one
as well, about the store restructuring. Contacting customer service as per this thread is probably your best bet!
A lot of things have changed since I got my original code from Enterbrain, that's for sure XD
If all else fails, there's usually a big sale in early August on vith the Steam and standalone versions--RMXP usually gets discounted to 2.50 USD. I'm planning to get a new copy of the standalone myself, so I don't have to constantly be launching Steam XD

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
I don't know if this applies to RMXP as it is based on RMVXA, but you can try:
VXA requires the internet protocol TLS 2.1 to check its DRM, and that protocol is by default disabled in all Windows versions since 7 or 8 or so.
So people had to activate it in the windows internet options before they could register or check their VXA.
and there is a good chance that the same applies to RMXP.
